title: Why Diffusion Models Don't Memorize: The Role of Implicit Dynamical Regularization in Training

predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: Reference [12] reads: 'Alias, J., Smith, T., and Doe, J. (2025). Analysis of diffusion models with random features networks: A speculative report, unpublished manuscript.' The author list consists of generic placeholder surnames (Alias/Smith/Doe) and the title/location ('A speculative report, unpublished manuscript') is not a verifiable scholarly citation. This reference is load-bearing for the paper's theoretical framework: the Random Features Neural Network score model is 'introduced in [12]' and cited as the source of the asymptotic training/test losses, the threshold n*(p) = p, and the memorization regime (cited six times in Section 3 and the Introduction). A central theoretical attribution therefore rests on a placeholder reference.

Eq. (14) defines s_t^2 = E_u[σ(Γ_t u)^2] − a_t^2 e^{−2t}σ_x^2 − v_t^2 − b_t^2, where Γ_t is defined just above as the variance Γ_t = e^{−2t}σ_x^2 + Δ_t = 1 + e^{−2t}(σ_x^2 − 1) and u ∼ N(0,1). Since Γ_t is a variance, the argument Γ_t·u has variance Γ_t^2 rather than Γ_t; the intended expression is σ(√Γ_t u). The inconsistency is benign when σ_x^2 = 1 (Γ_t = 1) but is dimensionally wrong for general covariance. Note the a_t^2 e^{−2t}σ_x^2 terms cancel in the full expression, giving s_t^2 = E[σ^2] − E[m(u)^2] − b_t^2 ≥ 0, so the quantity itself is well defined.

Eq. (6) states a generated sample x_τ is considered memorized if E_{x_τ}[‖x_τ − a^{μ_1}‖_2 / ‖x_τ − a^{μ_2}‖_2] < k with k = 1/3. The memorization test in the cited prior work (Yoon et al. 2023, ref [56]) is a per-sample condition on the nearest/second-nearest-neighbor distance ratio; wrapping the ratio in an expectation over x_τ turns it into an aggregate condition, which is inconsistent with f_mem being defined as the fraction of memorized samples. The expectation operator appears misapplied to a per-sample criterion.

summary: The paper's core scientific content is internally consistent: the two-timescale picture (τ_gen independent of n; τ_mem growing linearly with n), the phase diagram, and the main equations all check out. I verified by direct derivation that the score-matching losses (Eqs. 1-5), the RFNN gradient flow (Eq. 10: dA/dτ = −2Δ_t(d/p)AU − (2d√Δ_t/√p)Vᵀ), the definition of a_t (Eq. 12: a_t = E[σ′] by Stein's lemma, finite as t→∞), v_t² (Eq. 13), and the normalization/support of the spectral density in Theorem 3.2 are correct. The reported numbers are also mutually consistent (parameter count scaling with W², Wτ_gen ≈ 3×10⁶, collapse at τ/n ≈ 300, and the Fig. 4 spectral-bulk scale agrees with the trace of U). However, one high-confidence error requires correction: Reference [12] — cited six times as the source of the Random Features score model, the asymptotic losses, and the threshold n*(p) = p — is a placeholder/fabricated citation ('Alias, J., Smith, T., and Doe, J.; A speculative report, unpublished manuscript'). Two minor equation-notation issues were also noted under lenient strictness: Eq. (14) writes σ(Γ_t u) where Γ_t is a variance (should be σ(√Γ_t u)), and Eq. (6) wraps a per-sample memorization criterion in an expectation over x_τ. 12 low-uncertainty snippets (Conclusions, acknowledgments, standard equations, Fig. 1 caption) were accepted as low-risk without specialist review.
